project.title: Culture4All
project.description: Information visualization of access to culture across Italian regions, built on ISTAT and dati.cultura open data, with Corrado Consiglio and Salvatore Di Marzo.
project.introText: Culture for All maps access to culture across Italy: where libraries, archives and museums are, how people use libraries, and how reading habits differ from region to region.

gridImages.caption: Click any of 19,168 places for its record: here the Museo degli Innocenti, with hours, price and website from the Ministry of Culture's open data.
Places with free entry, counted in hexagons at country scale, in dark mode.
The supply map redraws from library counts to libraries per 10,000 inhabitants as you scroll.
Your place: Campania compared with Emilia-Romagna on every measure, with ranks and the Italian figure.

project.middleText: Built on open data from ISTAT and the Ministry of Culture, the 2026 version reads as an atlas of Italian culture: 19,168 libraries, museums, archives and heritage sites you can search, filter and click for their records; a supply map that turns counts into rates per inhabitant as you scroll; ranked comparisons of loans, reading and free entry; and a profile of any region or province against the Italian average. It is set in Fraunces and Source Serif on warm paper, with a light/dark switch.
project.conclusionText: Institutions cluster in Lombardy, Veneto, Tuscany and Lazio, cities borrow more than rural areas, and reading habits vary widely, which points to where cultural infrastructure needs investment. Made for Information Visualization (2023/24, University of Bologna) with Corrado Consiglio and Salvatore Di Marzo, who gathered and cleaned the data. I designed the visualisations and built the site with Leaflet, D3.js and Chart.js.
